headline: Watch: the Iran conflict and Strait of Hormuz disruption keep oil and fuel risk elevated, with no confirmed impacts on Australia.
summary: No material change since the last check. Hormuz shipping attacks continue, though oil eased to about US$95 after the US signalled restraint. Australia relies on imported fuel, so this remains the main path to SA, but no current shortage or rationing was found. The Ebola (Bundibugyo) outbreak in Africa is serious but distant, and there are no SA weather emergencies.
actions: Keep the car tank and any generator fuel at least half full while Hormuz shipping remains disrupted.

categories.name: Geopolitical & conflict
categories.summary: The US-Iran conflict and Hormuz shipping attacks continue, with the US signalling restraint if a deal is reached. Chinese military pressure around Taiwan remains a background concern; no new direct threat to Australia found.

sources.title: Oil falls as Trump signals restraint on Iran amid fresh Hormuz shipping attacks (TimesLIVE, 9 Nov)

categories.name: Nuclear & fallout
categories.summary: Iran's nuclear programme is part of negotiations, but there are no signs of nuclear use or alerts. No nuclear-command aircraft seen airborne by the collector.

categories.name: Cyber & infrastructure
categories.summary: No current major Australian outage or attack found; the Telstra nationwide outage in search results dates from July. CISA items are routine and the ACSC feed timed out.

sources.title: CISA: hardening industrial refrigeration and cold chain systems

categories.name: Pandemic & biological
categories.summary: The Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak has passed 10,600 confirmed cases in DR Congo, with imported cases in Kenya and Nigeria. Serious but distant; risk to SA is limited to rare imported cases.

sources.title: WHO Disease Outbreak News: Bundibugyo virus disease (6 Nov)

categories.name: Natural hazards
categories.summary: No GDACS orange/red alerts. The M6.4 Solomon Islands quake produced no tsunami. No current SA severe weather or bushfire emergencies found.

sources.title: USGS M6.4 – 30 km WSW of Lata, Solomon Islands

categories.name: Fuel, food & supply
categories.summary: Hormuz disruption keeps fuel supply tight after this year's shortages and refinery fire, but no current shortage or rationing was found.

sources.title: Oil falls on open as Trump says fresh Iran attacks unlikely (Reuters via Investing.com)

categories.name: Markets & finance
categories.summary: Brent down 3.3% to about US$95, VIX easing to 23, gold near record at US$4,118, AUD at 0.690. Stressed but calmer today.

concerns.title: US–Iran conflict & Hormuz shipping
drivers: Shipping attacks in and around the Strait of Hormuz are continuing, with a US blockade in place.
The US has signalled restraint if Iran reaches a deal; reports of softer Iranian demands are unconfirmed.
Brent oil eased to about US$95, but it is still high.

scenarios.name: Deal and de-escalation
scenarios.sa_impact: Fuel prices ease over weeks; no shortages.

scenarios.name: Grinding disruption continues
scenarios.sa_impact: Fuel stays expensive; occasional regional servo shortages like earlier this year.

scenarios.name: Major escalation or Hormuz closed
scenarios.sa_impact: Fuel rationing possible within 1–3 weeks; price spikes for food and freight.

actions.action: Keep car and generator fuel at least half full
actions.reason: Australia imports most of its fuel; in March hundreds of service stations ran dry within weeks of the Hormuz disruption.

actions.action: Hold a little cash at home
actions.reason: If fuel is rationed or networks fail, cash still works when cards may not.

concerns.title: Taiwan Strait / South China Sea
drivers: China's military pressure around Taiwan remains high after record drills this year.
Taiwan has reported a large Chinese naval presence; we could not confirm a current spike.

scenarios.name: Large drills or a 'quarantine' of Taiwan
scenarios.sa_impact: Shipping delays and market jitters; electronics and some medicines slower to arrive.

scenarios.name: Blockade or conflict
scenarios.sa_impact: Severe: most of Australia's fuel and many goods transit this region; Australian forces could be involved.

actions.reason: Nothing unusual is showing in the warning signs; the system will flag navigation warnings, GPS jamming or mobilisation reports if they appear.

concerns.title: Russia–NATO tensions
drivers: Reports of Russians leaving amid new draft fears.
Baltic and Black Sea GPS jamming is at its usual (high) level.

scenarios.name: Wider mobilisation or NATO incident
scenarios.sa_impact: Market shock and higher fuel prices; more cyber attacks globally.

scenarios.name: Direct Russia–NATO conflict
scenarios.sa_impact: Severe global market and energy shock; nuclear-risk rhetoric.

actions.action: Keep devices and banking apps updated
actions.reason: Russian-linked cyber campaigns spill over to Australian businesses and households during tense periods.

concerns.title: Ebola (Bundibugyo) outbreak in Africa
drivers: Over 10,600 confirmed cases in DR Congo, with imported cases in Kenya and Nigeria (WHO, 6 Nov).
No vaccine is approved for this strain.

scenarios.name: Stays largely in Central and East Africa
Imported cases in Europe or Asia
scenarios.sa_impact: Airport screening; low risk to SA.

scenarios.name: Case diagnosed in Australia
scenarios.sa_impact: Contained by public health response; small local risk.

actions.reason: Ebola spreads only through close contact with a sick person's body fluids; the risk in SA is very low.

concerns.title: Australian phone, internet & cyber disruption
drivers: All five monitored carriers are at normal levels.
No current major Australian cyber incident found.

scenarios.name: Nationwide carrier outage (like Optus 2023)
scenarios.sa_impact: Up to a day without mobile, NBN, EFTPOS or some 000 calls.

actions.action: Agree a family meeting point and save key numbers offline
actions.reason: In the 2023 Optus outage, millions could not call or pay for about 12 hours.
